subdivisions.name: Ohio
subdivisions.detail: Ohio applies a chance-weighted test ('game of chance' where the outcome is determined largely by chance) and has an active Casino Control Commission that has issued cease-and-desist letters to unlicensed operators. HB 298, which would legalise iGaming and ban sweepstakes, was pending in 2026. Ohio was a venue in the 2026 prediction-market loss-recovery class actions. Model C defensible if randomisation is stripped from the paid path; Model B unsettled and enforcement-exposed.
subdivisions.authority: O.R.C. s.2915.01(D) ('game of chance') and s.2915.02 (gambling) — text UNVERIFIED; Ohio HB 298 (pending). Regulator: Ohio Casino Control Commission; Ohio Attorney General.

subdivisions.name: Oklahoma
subdivisions.detail: S.B. 1589 — vetoed by Gov. Stitt on 7 May 2026 as 'vague and overbroad', VETO OVERRIDDEN 14 May 2026, effective 1 NOVEMBER 2026. Its definitions are the broadest of the 2026 wave: 'representative of value' means 'any and all currency used as part of a dual-currency system of payment that allows a person to exchange such currency for any prize, award, cash, or cash equivalent, OR ANY CHANCE TO WIN any prize, award, cash, or cash equivalent'. Liability extends to platform providers, payment and geolocation providers, gaming suppliers, promoters and affiliates. Class C2 felony. Oklahoma also grants tribal operators exclusive online gambling rights and is one of the eight states with no explicit agent-of-payee money-transmitter exemption. Absolute geofence for Model B. [AUDIT ADDITION] TRIBAL COMPACT EXPOSURE: state-tribal compact exclusivity gives tribes independent standing and enforcement leverage against unlicensed real-money gaming here, separate from the criminal code. Clearing the penal analysis does not clear a compact objection. Compact provisions UNVERIFIED. Oklahoma expressly grants tribal operators exclusive online gambling rights, which the brief noted but did not connect to compact-based enforcement standing.
subdivisions.authority: Okla. S.B. 1589 (2026), veto overridden 14 May 2026, eff. 1 Nov 2026; Okla. Stat. tit. 21 s.941 et seq. (gambling) — section detail UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Oklahoma Attorney General; Oklahoma Horse Racing Commission.

subdivisions.name: Oregon
subdivisions.detail: Material-element test and a specific internet-gambling provision. No enacted sweepstakes ban. Oregon is one of the eight states with NO explicit agent-of-payee money-transmitter exemption, so the custody structure is harder here. Model C defensible with randomisation removed; Model B unsettled.
subdivisions.authority: ORS s.167.117(7) ('contest of chance', material degree) and ORS s.167.109 (internet gambling) — text UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Oregon Department of Justice; Oregon Lottery.

subdivisions.name: Pennsylvania
subdivisions.detail: HOSTILE TO THE 'SKILL' FRAMING. In June 2026 the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that 'skill games' are slot machines under state law and must comply with the Commonwealth's gambling statutes, with enforcement stayed 120 days — making them illegal from 13 Oct 2026 unless the legislature acts. The AG obtained a $5m forfeiture and shutdown of two skill-game companies in April 2026 on felony corrupt-organisation pleas. That litigation concerns physical terminals, not online peer-to-peer contests, so it is not directly on point — but it is the clearest judicial statement anywhere that calling something a skill game does not take it out of gambling law. Pennsylvania has a full iGaming regulator. Model B: geofence. Model C: Pennsylvania opinion essential.
subdivisions.authority: 18 Pa.C.S. s.5513 (gambling devices) — text UNVERIFIED; Pennsylvania Supreme Court decision on skill games, June 2026 (case name and citation UNVERIFIED — reported by Spotlight PA). Regulator: Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board; Pennsylvania Attorney General.

subdivisions.name: Rhode Island
subdivisions.detail: No enacted sweepstakes ban and no verified skill-wagering statute, but Rhode Island has the lowest promotion-registration threshold in the country — reportedly $500 in total announced prize value for retail-linked games of chance, with no surety bond and no winners-list filing. Rhode Island is one of the eight states with NO explicit agent-of-payee money-transmitter exemption. Model C plausibly defensible; verify the registration trigger.
subdivisions.authority: R.I. Gen. Laws s.11-19-1 et seq. (gambling) — text UNVERIFIED; RI promotion registration threshold from secondary promotions-law sources. Regulator: Rhode Island Department of Business Regulation.

subdivisions.name: South Carolina
subdivisions.detail: South Carolina's unlawful-games-and-betting statute has been construed by the South Carolina Supreme Court in Town of Mt. Pleasant v. Chimento (2012) to reach games EVEN WHERE SKILL PREDOMINATES — the statutory meaning of 'gambling' in South Carolina includes games in which skill outweighs chance. H.4129 would amend the law to provide that paying a fee to play a skill-predominant game for a performance-proportionate prize is not gambling, but it has not passed. South Carolina also has a loss-recovery statute and was a venue in the 2026 prediction-market class actions. Blocked by Skillz. Absolute geofence. Footnote: South Carolina does not require a state money transmitter licence for most money-transmission activity.
subdivisions.authority: S.C. Code s.16-19-40 (unlawful games and betting); Town of Mt. Pleasant v. Chimento, 401 S.C. 522 (S.C. 2012) (citation partly UNVERIFIED); S.C. Code s.32-1-10 (loss recovery) — section UNVERIFIED; S.C. H.4129 (pending). Regulator: South Carolina Attorney General; SLED.

subdivisions.name: South Dakota
subdivisions.detail: South Dakota's internet-gambling chapter defines 'bet or wager' as taking, receiving or accepting money or any valuable thing on the understanding that it will be paid to a person if payment is contingent upon 'the result of a RACE, CONTEST, OR GAME or upon the happening of an event not known to be certain' — NO CHANCE ELEMENT IS REQUIRED, so a skill contest is squarely inside it. Establishing a location or site in the state from which to conduct a gambling business over the internet is a Class 6 FELONY (up to 2 years, $4,000), rising to Class 5 for repeat offences, and EACH INDIVIDUAL BET IS A SEPARATE VIOLATION. Blocked by Skillz. Absolute geofence. South Dakota adopted the MTMA.
subdivisions.authority: SDCL s.22-25A-1 ('bet or wager' defined); SDCL s.22-25A-8 (establishment of internet gambling business prohibited); SDCL s.22-25A-9 (each bet a separate violation). Regulator: South Dakota Commission on Gaming; South Dakota Attorney General.

subdivisions.name: Tennessee
subdivisions.detail: TWO INDEPENDENT PROHIBITIONS. (1) Tennessee defines gambling as 'risking anything of value for a profit whose return is TO ANY DEGREE CONTINGENT ON CHANCE' — effectively an any-chance test, with NO express skill exception in the definitions section. Randomised question selection alone is enough to engage it. This is the verified limb and it is sufficient on its own. (2) [CONTESTED — audit flagged at "possible" confidence] DATE UNVERIFIED: S.B. 2136, reported signed by Gov. Lee 22 May 2026 with immediate effect and no wind-down, prohibits online sweepstakes games using a virtual-, dual- or multi-currency system exchangeable for cash, prizes or anything of value that simulate casino-style gambling; violations are unfair or deceptive acts under the Tennessee Consumer Protection Act with AG investigative authority. The Act also targets prediction markets. Confirm the signing date and immediate-effect characterisation from the enrolled bill. Blocked by Skillz. Absolute geofence — limb (1) alone justifies it.
subdivisions.authority: Tenn. Code Ann. s.39-17-501(1) (definition of 'gambling', 2024 Tennessee Code in force — VERIFIED limb); Tenn. S.B. 2136 / H.B. 1885 — signing date and immediate effect UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Tennessee Attorney General; Tennessee Sports Wagering Council.

subdivisions.name: Texas
subdivisions.detail: Texas criminalises making a bet on the partial or final result of a game or contest or on the performance of a participant. There is a social-gambling defence — private place, no economic benefit other than personal winnings, equal odds for all participants — but it is UNAVAILABLE TO AN OPERATOR that takes a fee or rake, which is the whole business model. SB 517 (redefining gambling devices) failed in 2026. Texas has no gaming regulator and enforcement is by district attorneys, which makes exposure unpredictable rather than absent. Model B: geofence on a conservative read. Model C: Texas opinion needed, focused on whether an operator-funded fixed prize is a 'bet'.
subdivisions.authority: Tex. Penal Code s.47.01(1) ('bet') and s.47.02 (gambling; social-gambling defence at s.47.02(b)) — text UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Texas Attorney General; local district attorneys.

subdivisions.name: Utah
subdivisions.detail: Utah is the most absolutist gambling state in the country. 'Gambling' means 'RISKING ANYTHING OF VALUE FOR A RETURN or risking anything of value upon the outcome of a contest, game, gaming scheme, or gaming device when the return or outcome is based on an element of chance' — note that the FIRST clause carries no chance qualifier at all. Combined with the constitutional prohibition, there is no lawful gambling of any kind in Utah and no regulator to licence you. Utah is also one of the eight states with NO explicit agent-of-payee money-transmitter exemption. Operator-level restrictions on sweepstakes platforms already reported. Absolute geofence for Models B and C.
subdivisions.authority: Utah Code Ann. s.76-10-1101(2) (definition of 'gambling', 2024 Utah Code in force); Utah Const. art. VI s.27. Regulator: Utah Attorney General.

subdivisions.name: Vermont
subdivisions.detail: Vermont permits persons to organise, execute or participate in contests or sweepstakes PROVIDED THAT persons who enter are NOT REQUIRED TO VENTURE MONEY OR OTHER VALUABLE THINGS. On that wording, paid entry disqualifies the contest — the same structural bar as Montana. Vermont is easy to miss because it appears on no sweepstakes-ban list. No enacted online sweepstakes ban. Geofence Models B and C pending verification.
subdivisions.authority: 13 V.S.A. s.2143b (contests and sweepstakes) — quoted text obtained from a Justia/Vermont Legislature listing summary; DIRECT FETCH FAILED, so treat the quotation as strong but RE-VERIFY before relying. 13 V.S.A. ch. 51 (gambling and lotteries). Regulator: Vermont Attorney General; Vermont Department of Liquor and Lottery.

subdivisions.name: Virginia
subdivisions.detail: Virginia's illegal-gambling definition turns on an outcome dependent on chance and is generally understood to carry an exception for a contest of speed or skill between men, animals, fowl or vehicles where participants may receive prizes — which would support Model C. Gov. Spanberger VETOED legislation to legalise electronic skill gaming devices in April 2026, and HB 161 (iGaming plus sweepstakes ban) failed in the 2026 session; SB 579 would categorise unlicensed online sweepstakes games as illegal gambling with civil penalties of $10,000-$100,000 per violation. Separately relevant to Model D: Virginia's automatic-renewal amendments take effect 1 Jul 2026, requiring an online cancel path at least as easy as sign-up. Monitor — Virginia is likely to enact a sweepstakes ban.
subdivisions.authority: Va. Code s.18.2-325 (definitions) and s.18.2-334 (exception for contests of speed or skill) — text UNVERIFIED; Va. SB 579 (2026, pending); Virginia automatic renewal law amendments eff. 1 Jul 2026 (bill number UNVERIFIED). Regulator: Virginia Lottery Board / Virginia Gaming Commission; Virginia Attorney General.

subdivisions.name: Washington
subdivisions.detail: THE MOST DANGEROUS STATE IN THE UNION FOR THIS PRODUCT, AND THE ONE THAT REACHES MODEL A. (1) Operating internet gambling — knowingly transmitting or receiving gambling information over the internet — is a CLASS C FELONY. (2) 'Thing of value' expressly includes 'any form of credit or promise ... involving extension of a service, entertainment or a privilege of playing at a game or scheme without charge'. In Kater v. Churchill Downs Inc., 886 F.3d 784 (9th Cir. 28 Mar 2018), the Ninth Circuit held Big Fish Casino's virtual chips were a 'thing of value' on exactly that basis, because without chips a user cannot play — making the free-to-play social casino illegal gambling under Washington law. The related claims settled for a reported $155m. (3) The 'contest of chance' test is material-degree, so randomised question draws are enough. (4) Washington's Recovery of Money Lost at Gambling Act gives every Washington player a private right to recover losses. (5) Sweepstakes trackers list Washington, with Idaho, as already prohibiting the dual-currency model under pre-existing law. GEOFENCE WASHINGTON FOR EVERY MODEL THAT INVOLVES STAKING PURCHASED COINS, INCLUDING MODEL A. Footnote: Washington's money-transmitter surety bond minimum is among the lowest at $10,000.
subdivisions.authority: Wash. Rev. Code s.9.46.240 (internet gambling, Class C felony); s.9.46.0285 ('thing of value'); s.9.46.0237 ('gambling'); s.9.46.0225 ('contest of chance', material degree); RCW s.4.24.070 (recovery of money lost at gambling); Kater v. Churchill Downs Inc., 886 F.3d 784 (9th Cir. 2018). Regulator: Washington State Gambling Commission.

subdivisions.name: West Virginia
subdivisions.detail: No enacted sweepstakes ban and no verified skill-wagering prohibition. West Virginia has a full iGaming regulator and permits esports wagering, which signals that paid-entry skill contests are regulable rather than per se criminal. Model C plausibly defensible; Model B unsettled.
subdivisions.authority: W. Va. Code s.61-10-1 et seq. (gaming) — text UNVERIFIED. Regulator: West Virginia Lottery Commission.

subdivisions.name: Wisconsin
subdivisions.detail: Wisconsin's 'bet' definition is chance-based with exclusions for bona fide business transactions and, on the usual model-penal-code pattern, for bona fide contests of skill, speed, strength or endurance — but I could not verify the exclusion text. No enacted sweepstakes ban. Wisconsin adopted the MTMA. Model C plausibly defensible; verify before launch.
subdivisions.authority: Wis. Stat. s.945.01(1) ('bet') and exclusions — text UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Wisconsin Department of Administration, Division of Gaming.

subdivisions.name: Wyoming
subdivisions.detail: Wyoming's gambling definition turns on gain 'contingent in whole or in part upon lot, chance, the operation of a gambling device' and is generally understood to exclude bona fide contests of skill, speed, strength or endurance in which awards are made only to entrants or the owners of entries — one of the more permissive framings. No enacted sweepstakes ban. Wyoming is one of the eight states with NO explicit agent-of-payee money-transmitter exemption, but its money-transmitter surety bond minimum is among the lowest at $10,000. Model C plausibly the most permissive state; verify the skill exclusion text.
subdivisions.authority: Wyo. Stat. s.6-7-101(a)(iii) (definition of 'gambling' and skill-contest exclusion) — text UNVERIFIED. Regulator: Wyoming Gaming Commission.

risks: THE SKILL ARGUMENT DOES NOT SAVE MODEL B. CORRECTED COUNT: TEN states, not eleven, legislate around the skill/chance question — Arizona (gambling includes contests 'of chance or skill'), California Penal Code s.337a(a)(6) (bets on contests of skill BETWEEN PERSONS), Florida s.849.14, Delaware 11 Del. C. s.1403, Illinois 720 ILCS 5/28-1(a)(1) ('game of chance or skill'), Louisiana R.S. 14:90 (no chance element at all), Nevada NRS 463.0152 (no skill/chance distinction), South Dakota SDCL s.22-25A-1 (contest or game, no chance element), South Carolina (Chimento), Arkansas s.5-66-104. MONTANA IS REMOVED: the brief's Mont. Code Ann. s.23-5-110 'paid entry disqualifies a skill contest' claim is withdrawn — that section is 'Public policy of state concerning gambling' and defines nothing, and Montana's actual gambling definition at s.23-5-112(14)(a) is chance-based (both verified at mca.legmt.gov, 14 Sep 2026). Any pitch deck or investor memo that says 'trivia is skill so we are fine' is still wrong on the law in the remaining ten.

YOUR VENDORS GO DOWN WITH YOU. California Penal Code s.337o, New York Rac. Pari-Mut. Wag. & Breeding L. s.912 and Oklahoma S.B. 1589 all extend criminal or civil liability to payment processors, financial institutions, geolocation providers, content and technology suppliers, platform providers, promoters and MEDIA AFFILIATES who knowingly support a prohibited operator. The practical consequence is not that you get prosecuted first — it is that no reputable PSP, geolocation vendor or affiliate network will onboard you, and any that does will terminate on first notice, stranding player balances mid-contest.

PRIVATE LOSS-RECOVERY LITIGATION IS A BIGGER THREAT THAN PROSECUTION. Illinois 720 ILCS 5/28-8 (recover losses of $50+); KENTUCKY — CORRECTED — KRS 372.020 (the loser's own action, $5+) AND THE SEPARATE KRS 372.040 (after six months, ANY OTHER PERSON may sue for TREBLE the loss); Washington RCW 4.24.070; plus analogues in Georgia, South Carolina, Massachusetts and Ohio. s.372.040 is the provision that creates the real exposure: it turns a private remedy into a bounty available to strangers and litigation funders. These need no conviction, no regulator and no intent — just a player who lost money on an unlicensed game. The Kater line settled for a reported $155m. The 2026 class actions against Kalshi, Robinhood and Webull used exactly this machinery across five states at once, funded by a litigation-finance firm. [AUDIT ADDITION] An arbitration clause and class-action waiver are the standard mitigation but do not reliably bind users below the age of majority — 19 in Alabama and Nebraska, 21 in Mississippi.

WASHINGTON AND NEW YORK REACH MODEL A. RCW 9.46.0285 and N.Y. Penal Law s.225.00(6) ('Something of value' — CORRECTED from the brief's s.225.00(1), which is 'Contest of chance'; verified at nysenate.gov 14 Sep 2026) both define a thing of value to include the privilege of playing a game without charge. Kater v. Churchill Downs (9th Cir. 2018) applied that to virtual chips. FACT//DUEL's existing demo-coin escrow — coins staked into escrow, winner takes the escrow — is structurally the same mechanic. If those coins ever become purchasable, the product is arguably illegal gambling in Washington with no cash-out feature at all. The fix is architectural and must be designed in now: purchased coins must be spend-only and structurally incapable of being staked.

THE 2026 LEGISLATIVE WAVE IS NOT OVER. CORRECTED: about TEN states enacted express dual-currency prohibitions between June 2025 and November 2026 (CA, CT, IN, LA, ME, MT, NJ, NY, OK, TN), and TWO more (IA, NV) granted regulators open-ended enforcement authority without defining the offence. Bills failed but will return in Minnesota, Florida, Massachusetts, Mississippi, Hawaii, Texas and Arkansas; bills are live in DC, Ohio, Virginia, Maryland and Missouri. A compliance posture built on today's map will be out of date within one legislative session. Budget for ongoing monitoring, and build the geofence as a configuration table with a per-state effective-date column, not as hard-coded logic. [AUDIT ADDITION] As at 14 Sep 2026 Oklahoma (1 Nov 2026) is the ONLY listed prohibition not yet operative — do not stage a launch into that seven-week window.

MOST SWEEPSTAKES BANS REQUIRE THE GAME TO 'SIMULATE CASINO-STYLE GAMBLING', AND A TRIVIA DUEL PROBABLY DOES NOT — BUT DO NOT BUILD ON THAT GAP. It is untested, it is a question of characterisation that a hostile AG will resolve against you, Oklahoma's 'representative of value' definition is drafted broadly enough to reach any dual-currency exchangeable for any chance to win, Iowa's S.F. 2289 is a pure enforcement grant with no definitional limit at all, and California s.337a(a)(6) and Florida s.849.14 close the gap independently of any sweepstakes ban.

MONEY TRANSMISSION IS THE HIDDEN COST CENTRE — BUT CORRECTED, AND THE CORRECTION CUTS IN THE FOUNDER'S FAVOUR FOR MODEL C. State MTL regimes, and the CSBS MTMA definition, generally turn on receiving money FOR TRANSMISSION TO ANOTHER PERSON. Model B — holding one player's stake for payment to another player — squarely raises money transmission and, if required across the country, means licences in 49 states plus DC: fees $500-$10,000 per state, bonds from $10,000 to $500,000 (California scaling to $7m), tangible net worth the greater of $100,000 or 3% of assets, 3-12 months per state and 12-18+ for New York and California. That is a multi-year, seven-figure programme and it is effectively disqualifying for a startup. Model C — operator-funded, fixed, entrant-count-independent prizes paid from the operator's own funds — is frequently NOT transmission to a third party and may fall outside the definition entirely in many states. The brief collapsed the two and called a 49-state programme 'the single largest cost and time line item in the whole plan' for both, which materially overstates the burden for the design it recommends. Get a money-transmission opinion on the threshold question before assuming the programme exists. The MTMA harmonises standards, not licences, and its adopter count as stated in the brief was internally inconsistent and is UNVERIFIED. The safest structure remains never taking custody, via a licensed PSP or sponsor bank.

APP STORE POLICY MAY BE A HARDER GATE THAN STATE LAW. Both Apple and Google require real-money gaming apps to be submitted by the licensed entity and geo-restricted to licensed territories. CORRECTED: the reason is not that no licence exists anywhere — Nevada NRS 463.160 and New Jersey's DGE esports event wagering licence are real categories — but that none of them fits a peer-to-peer mobile trivia app at viable cost or lead time, so there is no licence you can actually show the stores. Model B may simply be unshippable on either store regardless of how the state analysis comes out. Confirm current store policy directly before spending on legal opinions.

THE PRODUCT'S CURRENT MECHANICS ARE THE WORST-CASE FACTS. A 5/7/10-second timer compresses the skill window and amplifies reaction-time variance; randomised question sets introduce a draw-luck element; Expeditions stake at three confidence tiers on rotating question sets, which reads as a wager on an uncertain outcome; and matchmaking determines your opponent. Each of those is a chance input a prosecutor or plaintiff will point to under a material-element test. If real money is ever introduced, the paid path must be redesigned: identical question sets for all entrants, no confidence-tier variance, and a fixed operator-funded prize.

NO STATE OFFERS A COMMERCIALLY VIABLE LICENCE FOR THIS — CORRECTED FROM 'NO STATE LICENSES THIS'. The brief stated a categorical 51-jurisdiction absolute that its own Nevada entry contradicted. Licensure exists in principle: Nevada NRS 463.0152 defines a gambling game as any game played for money with NO skill/chance distinction and NRS 463.160 licenses exactly that, and New Jersey's DGE licenses esports event wagering. What is true is that no state has an OFF-THE-SHELF licence category that fits a peer-to-peer mobile trivia app at viable cost and lead time: the categories that exist are casino, sports wagering, fantasy sports, lottery, charitable gaming and, in a handful of states, esports wagering, and a Nevada non-restricted licence is a multi-year, multi-million-dollar suitability process. The practical conclusion for a startup is unchanged — 'lawful-only-with-licence' is not a path you can fund — but the claim must be stated accurately, because an investor or counsel will find the Nevada contradiction immediately.

[AUDIT ADDITION] TRIBAL GAMING COMPACTS ARE A STATE-LAYER RISK THE ORIGINAL BRIEF NEVER MENTIONED. Exclusivity provisions in state-tribal compacts in California, Florida, Oklahoma and Connecticut give tribes independent standing and enforcement leverage against unlicensed real-money gaming. Tribal objection has killed products that had a clean reading of the state criminal code, and it arrives through a different channel — compact dispute mechanisms, federal court, and political pressure on the state regulator — so a clean penal-code opinion does not dispose of it. Oklahoma additionally grants tribal operators exclusive online gambling rights. Compact provisions and their reach to a non-casino skill product: UNVERIFIED. Scope the gaming-counsel engagement to cover it.

[AUDIT ADDITION] UNCLAIMED PROPERTY IS A LIVE OBLIGATION FOR THE TWO MODELS THE BRIEF CLEARED AS 'LAWFUL'. Models A and D both accumulate stored value in unredeemed coin and credit balances. Several states treat unredeemed prepaid balances as ABANDONED PROPERTY with reporting and remittance duties to the state treasurer after a dormancy period. The brief cleared A and D with no caveat beyond in-app-purchase disclosure. The engineering consequence is immediate even though the legal one is not: you need a server-authoritative per-user balance ledger with last-activity timestamps, which FACT//DUEL's local-only IndexedDB store cannot provide. Per-state thresholds, dormancy periods and whether closed-loop non-redeemable game currency is exempt: UNVERIFIED.

[AUDIT ADDITION] GEOFENCING THE COMPANY IS NOT THE SAME AS PROTECTING THE USER. Several statutes this lane relies on reach the person who PLAYS OR BETS, not only the operator — 720 ILCS 5/28-1(a)(1) and Cal. Penal Code s.337a among them. The brief disentangled the two only for Illinois. Whoever writes the terms of service needs to know, per state, whether the block list protects the company, the user, or both, because it determines the refund posture, whether a balance must be returned to a user who played from a prohibited state, and what the product may truthfully tell users about their own exposure. Per-state scope: UNVERIFIED.

[AUDIT ADDITION] THE FREE-ENTRY (AMOE) ROUTE IS THE MOST LEGISLATIVELY TARGETED STRUCTURE IN THE COUNTRY RIGHT NOW. The brief jumped from Model B to Model C without evaluating whether a genuine alternative method of entry would remove the consideration element and open more states — the structure the sweepstakes industry actually uses. It is a real option and leaving it unmapped leaves the strategy space incomplete. But the decisive fact is that the ENTIRE 2025-26 dual-currency ban wave catalogued in this lane exists precisely BECAUSE operators used an AMOE to argue they were not gambling. An AMOE is legitimate for a promotional contest; it is not a safe harbour in 2026, and it does not help at all in states whose prohibition does not turn on consideration (AZ, FL, DE, SD, LA). Cost it before committing; do not adopt it without a per-state opinion. UNVERIFIED as to which states it opens.

COLORADO AND NEBRASKA CONFLICT: model-penal-code-derived gambling definitions appear to exclude bona fide skill contests where awards go only to entrants, but promotions-law compliance guides list both states as barring consideration in contests. I could not reconcile these from primary sources. The conflict probably reflects two different bodies of law (criminal gambling vs. consumer-protection prize-promotion rules) applying to the same facts, which would mean both are true and both must be satisfied — but that is an inference, not a verified finding.

MARYLAND CRIM. LAW s.12-114 — a secondary source (Legal Moves Law Firm) characterised this as recognising esports as lawful skill contests generally. The statutory text I read is narrower: it covers 'a competition involving video games, including first-person shooters, real-time strategy games, and multiplayer online battle arenas'. A trivia app is unlikely to qualify. Do not rely on the broader characterisation.
